```{r, include = FALSE}
# Executed chunks are wrapped so the site can run them in the browser with webR.
knitr::knit_hooks$set(webr = function(before, options) if (before) "\n<div class=\"webr-chunk\">\n" else "\n</div>\n")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", webr = TRUE,
                      fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4, fig.align = "center",
                      out.width = "100%", dpi = 110)
options(width = 76)
```

This guide goes from the study to report-ready tables and figures. It
uses the simulated two-arm trial, so every result below is reproducible,
and you can press **Run** to execute any chunk in your browser.

<div class="webr-panel">

**What is `nx`?** `nx` is the name these guides give to the project
**engine**: the object returned by `cdmstat_demo()`, `cdmstat_connect()` or
`cdmstat_setup()`. It is not a dataset. It holds the connection, the
cached data, the data dictionary and the audit ledger, and you ask it for
things with `$`, e.g. `nx$table_one()` or `nx$fit()`. You can call it
anything, for example `trial <- cdmstat_demo()`.

Datasets come out of the engine as ordinary data frames, under names *you*
choose. Here, `wide` is one row per subject and `long` is one row per
subject and visit. Column names follow the REDCap fields: `sbp` in long
data, and `sbp__week_24` (field, two underscores, visit) in wide data.

</div>

## 1. Open the study

```{r}
library(REDCapCDMSTAT)
library(ggplot2)

# The engine for the simulated trial (a real study: cdmstat_setup()).
nx <- cdmstat_demo(dir = file.path(tempdir(), "stats"),
                   reset = TRUE, actor = "sam")

# Arm colours used in every plot below.
arm_cols <- c("Drug A" = "#A01621", "Placebo" = "#2C5D8F")
```

## 2. Analysis datasets

```{r}
# One row per subject: visit fields become field__visit columns, and the
# repeating adverse-event form is summarised (n_, any_, max_ columns).
wide <- nx$shape(longitudinal = "wide", repeating = "collapse")

# One row per subject and visit, for repeated-measures analyses.
# carry_constant copies subject-level fields (arm, age, ...) to
# every visit row; in REDCap they are recorded only at baseline.
long <- nx$shape(longitudinal = "long", repeating = "drop",
                 carry_constant = TRUE)

c(subjects = nrow(wide), visit_rows = nrow(long))

# What was created, with labels from the data dictionary.
vars <- attr(wide, "variables")
head(vars[vars$type != "id", c("name", "type", "label")], 8)
```

## 3. Table 1

The treatment arm and the baseline variables are found in the data
dictionary. CDMSTAT chooses each summary and test from the data
(Shapiro-Wilk normality, expected cell counts), and gtsummary lays the
table out:

```{r}
# Baseline characteristics by randomised arm, with p-values.
nx$table_one_gt()
```

Why each test was chosen:

```{r}
t1 <- nx$table_one()
why <- t1[nzchar(t1$test), c("label", "test", "rationale")]
knitr::kable(why, row.names = FALSE)
```

For a confirmatory analysis, pre-specify the tests from the statistical
analysis plan and use `mode = "sap"`. CDMSTAT then refuses any variable
without one:

```{r}
nx$table_one_gt(vars = c("age", "sex", "sbp"),
                tests = list(age = "wilcox", sex = "chisq",
                             sbp = "t.test"),
                mode = "sap")
```

## 4. Look at the data

### Baseline distributions

```{r baseline-box}
base <- long[long$redcap_event_name == "baseline_arm_1", ]

ggplot(base, aes(arm, sbp, colour = arm)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.5) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.5, size = 1.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = arm_cols, guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Systolic BP at baseline (mmHg)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

### Individual trajectories and arm means

```{r trajectories, fig.height = 4.4}
# Visit order and readable names from the study's event schedule.
ev <- nx$events
long$visit <- factor(long$redcap_event_name,
                     levels = ev$unique_event_name,
                     labels = ev$event_name)

# Arm means with 95% confidence intervals.
tr <- nx$trend("sbp")
tr$visit <- factor(tr$event, levels = ev$unique_event_name,
                   labels = ev$event_name)
names(tr)[names(tr) == "group"] <- "arm"

ggplot(long, aes(visit, sbp, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = record_id), alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_pointrange(data = tr, aes(y = mean, ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), size = 0.5) +
  geom_line(data = tr, aes(y = mean, group = arm), linewidth = 1,
            position = position_dodge(width = 0.3)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = arm_cols) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(90, 180)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Systolic BP (mmHg)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Outliers become queries

```{r outliers}
# Robust z-scores within each visit; |z| > 3 is flagged.
o <- nx$outliers("weight")
long$flag <- o$outlier[match(paste(long$record_id, long$redcap_event_name),
                             paste(o$record_id, o$event))]

ggplot(long, aes(height, weight)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = flag %in% TRUE), alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_text(data = long[long$flag %in% TRUE, ],
            aes(label = paste("record", record_id)),
            hjust = -0.15, size = 3.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey60", `TRUE` = "#A01621"),
                      labels = c("within range", "outlier"),
                      name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Height (cm)", y = "Weight (kg)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Each flagged point can be raised as a query in one line, which is what
clicking the point does in the apps:

```{r}
nx$add_query("7", "weight", "Weight 450 kg is implausible",
             event = "baseline_arm_1", value = "450",
             source = "analysis")
```

### Time to the primary endpoint

```{r km, fig.height = 4.6}
km <- ggsurvfit::survfit2(
  survival::Surv(followup_days, event_occurred == "Yes") ~ arm,
  data = wide)

ggsurvfit::ggsurvfit(km, linewidth = 1) +
  ggsurvfit::add_confidence_interval() +
  ggsurvfit::add_risktable() +
  scale_colour_manual(values = unname(arm_cols)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = unname(arm_cols)) +
  labs(x = "Days since randomisation", y = "Event-free probability") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Adverse events

```{r ae}
ae <- nx$shape(repeating = "only")
ae$arm <- wide$arm[match(ae$record_id, wide$record_id)]

ggplot(ae, aes(y = ae_term, fill = arm)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = arm_cols) +
  labs(x = "Adverse events (n)", y = "Reported term (verbatim)",
       fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## 5. Models

`nx$fit()` fits the model on the shaped data and `tbl_fit()` formats it
for a report, with dictionary labels and, for logistic and Cox models,
odds and hazard ratios.

**ANCOVA**: week-24 systolic BP adjusted for baseline.

```{r}
ancova <- nx$fit("sbp__week_24 ~ arm + sbp__baseline", "linear")
tbl_fit(ancova)
```

**Logistic regression**: any serious adverse event.

```{r}
logit <- nx$fit("any_ae_serious ~ arm + age", "logistic")
tbl_fit(logit)
```

**Cox regression**: time to the primary endpoint.

```{r}
cox <- nx$fit(
  "Surv(followup_days, event_occurred == 'Yes') ~ arm + age", "cox")
tbl_fit(cox)
```

**Mixed model** for the repeated blood-pressure measurements, with a random
intercept per subject:

```{r}
mm <- nx$fit("sbp ~ arm * redcap_event_name + (1 | record_id)",
             "mixed")
tbl_fit(mm)
```

### Treatment effect over time

The mixed model gives the Placebo minus Drug A difference at each visit,
combining the main effect with the visit interaction:

```{r effect-plot, fig.height = 3.4}
m <- attr(mm, "model")
b <- lme4::fixef(m)
V <- as.matrix(stats::vcov(m))

# Contrast for each visit: arm effect + arm-by-visit interaction.
L <- sapply(ev$unique_event_name, function(e) {
  w <- as.numeric(names(b) == "armPlacebo")
  int <- paste0("armPlacebo:redcap_event_name", e)
  if (int %in% names(b)) w[names(b) == int] <- 1
  w
})
est <- drop(t(L) %*% b)
se <- sqrt(diag(t(L) %*% V %*% L))
eff <- data.frame(visit = factor(ev$event_name, levels = ev$event_name),
                  est, lo = est - 1.96 * se, hi = est + 1.96 * se)

ggplot(eff, aes(visit, est, ymin = lo, ymax = hi)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_pointrange(colour = "#A01621", linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Placebo minus Drug A\nsystolic BP (mmHg, 95% CI)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

By chance, the placebo arm starts about 6 mmHg lower than Drug A at
baseline. By week 24 it is about 3 mmHg higher, because systolic BP falls on
Drug A and not on placebo. The difference in change from baseline to week
24 is the `Placebo * Week 24` term in the table above, about 9 mmHg. That
is the simulated drug effect.

## 6. Reproducibility

Every analytic call above was logged. `nx$script()` returns a linear R
script that replays them. The script connects to the study from the
environment, so it never contains a token:

```{r}
cat(tail(strsplit(nx$script(), "\n")[[1]], 10), sep = "\n")
```

To pin an analysis to a frozen, signed-off dataset, call
`nx$use_cut(cut_id, require_signoff = TRUE)` first; see
[Reports, CDISC and reproducibility](reports-cdisc.html).
